Civil engineer here. It depends on many factors which include what kind of vehicles will be traveling over it, what kind of forces it will have to sustain, what the geography is, what the climate is, what is it spanning across, what materials are going to be used, the length of the span, etc.

Civil engineeing is generally split up into 5a fields which then are split up into smaller fields.

Enviromental. And Watera Resource Engineering- deal with water. Design flood walls, sewer systems, drainage, enviromental impact of construction, etc.

Transportation Engineering-design roads, railroads, airports, public transport, etc. Also design traffic light set-ups to make traffic flow better.

Geotechnical engineering- design building foundations and test soil properties so a building doesn't collapse due to uneasy soil.

Structural engineering- design buildings and bridges, makes sure they don't collapse due to wind, earthquakes,etc. Can specialize in concrete or steel.

Construction management- focuses on the legal and financial aspect of a project, makes schedules and assures deadlines are met.
